name: Internal Monologue - NTLM Hash Extraction Without Touching LSASS
description: Internal Monologue extracts NTLM hashes by triggering local NTLM challenges against logged-in users via the SSPI API, without reading LSASS memory. It forces a NetNTLMv1 downgrade (if possible) to get crackable hashes, or captures NetNTLMv2 hashes. This bypasses credential guard and most EDR detections that monitor LSASS access.
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
Instead of reading LSASS memory (which EDR detects), Internal
Monologue uses the SSPI API to initiate a local NTLM authentication
challenge. The response contains the users hash.

=== RUN ===
  InternalMonologue.exe -Downgrade True -Restore True -Impersonate True -Verbose True
  # -Downgrade: Force NTLMv1 (easier to crack)
  # -Restore: Restore NTLMv1 setting after
  # -Impersonate: Get hashes for all logged-in users

=== OUTPUT ===
  # NetNTLMv1 (if downgrade successful):
  user::domain:challenge:response:response
  # Crack with hashcat -m 5500

  # NetNTLMv2 (if downgrade blocked):
  user::domain:challenge:response:response
  # Crack with hashcat -m 5600

=== WHY ITS STEALTHY ===
- Does NOT open LSASS process
- Does NOT inject into LSASS
- Does NOT touch SAM/SECURITY hives
- Uses legitimate SSPI API calls
- Most EDRs dont flag it

=== REQUIREMENTS ===
- Local admin (for impersonation and NTLMv1 downgrade)
- Users must be currently logged in
- Works even with Credential Guard enabled

=== ALTERNATIVE: Inveigh ===
Inveigh can also capture NetNTLMv2 hashes via LLMNR/mDNS poisoning.

examples.label: Extract hashes for all logged-in users

recommended.note: Inveigh captures hashes via network poisoning; Internal Monologue via local SSPI.

defense.why_it_works: The Windows SSPI API allows local processes to initiate NTLM authentication challenges. By impersonating logged-in users and triggering local challenges, their NTLM hashes can be extracted without accessing LSASS memory.
defense.prerequisites: Local admin on the target machine; users must be logged in.
defense.impact: NTLM hash extraction for all logged-in users; enables offline cracking or pass-the-hash.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1003] NTLMv1 downgrade (LmCompatibilityLevel change); unusual SSPI authentication events; registry modifications.
defense.artifacts: Registry change to LmCompatibilityLevel; NTLM authentication events; token impersonation.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=13 TargetObject="*\Control\Lsa\LmCompatibilityLevel"
| table _time, Image, TargetObject, Details
defense.sentinel_kql:
SysmonEvent
| where EventID == 13
| where RegistryKey has "LmCompatibilityLevel"
| project TimeGenerated, Image, RegistryKey, RegistryValue
defense.prevention: Enforce NTLMv2-only via GPO (LmCompatibilityLevel=5); disable NTLM entirely where possible; monitor for LmCompatibilityLevel changes; use Credential Guard.

detections.name: NTLMv1 downgrade for Internal Monologue
detections.logic:
SysmonEvent
| where EventID == 13
| where RegistryKey has "LmCompatibilityLevel"
| where RegistryValue in ("0", "1", "2")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Image, RegistryKey, RegistryValue
detections.false_positives: Legacy application compatibility changes; Group Policy updates
detections.tuning: Alert on any LmCompatibilityLevel change below 3; correlate with token impersonation events
